title: Briefing: Albania, Canada, India, Italy, France and South Africa
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Friday, October thirtieth. It's narrated by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.

Albania. The Guardian reports that Albania's government adopted legislative measures imposing fines of up to 500,000 leks for individuals who remain in a crowd where violence, looting, or identity concealment occurs. Reported so far by one source.

Canada. British Columbia's Conservative Party wins a majority government in the snap election Premier David Eby called for October twenty-fourth, in which the pipeline was a campaign issue, CTV News declares. Confirmed by independent reports.

India. Freddy Francis, who helped found the CJP's Kerala unit, says he has quit any official role in it, citing "serious disagreements" over the unit's fundraising practices and what he calls immature political statements he felt undermined the movement's character. Reported so far by one source.

Italy. The Associated Press separately reports police arrested 45 people over the two nights of Milan violence, 34 of them minors, as roughly 2,000 very young people took part in the looting and clashes. Reported so far by one source.

France. The interior ministry says 410,000 people protested nationwide on Saturday, including 110,000 in Paris, in marches over the cost of living and the high-school movement; the CGT union puts both figures at nearly double the official count. Reported so far by one source.

South Africa. Police arrest five men, aged 19 to 46, outside the Home Affairs offices on Che Guevara Road in Umbilo as persons of interest in the murder, attempted murder and assault cases linked to the unrest, Netshiunda says, IOL reports. Reported so far by one source.

Albania's student protests. The Guardian reports that the leaderless protest movement began peacefully in May with rallies against a luxury hotel project in a nature reserve backed by the US president's son-in-law Jared Kushner, before morphing into student-led anti-government protests in mid-October. That's reported so far by one source.
South Africa's asylum ruling unrest. Coming up: local government elections on November fourth.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
